title: Transient cohort feature toggle with SLO-aware fallback and auto-heal
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation:
We need a rollout primitive that lets product teams enable a model variant for short-lived, controlled cohorts (minutes->hours) tied to a feature flag, with automatic SLO-aware fallback and an auto-heal path. Existing staged canaries and shadowing are heavyweight for short experiments and add operational overhead (manual quarantines, long TTLs). This PR introduces a transient cohort toggle controller and runtime integration that: 1) assigns requests to ephemeral cohorts based on feature-flag evaluation and sampling policy, 2) enforces SLO gates (p95 latency, error-rate) per-cohort and triggers immediate fallback if thresholds breach, and 3) supports an automatic heal that attempts gradual re-admittance after a cool-down window.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a transient cohort controller (pkg/rollout/transient_cohort.go) that takes feature-flag headers or SDK-evaluated flags and maps them to short-lived cohort state stored in the rollout store.
- Adds SLO gate hooks to the request router (pkg/serving/slo_gate_integration.go) to evaluate per-cohort metrics in streaming fashion and execute fallback actions (route to baseline model, serve degraded mode) when gates are tripped.
- Implements auto-heal logic (pkg/rollout/auto_heal.go) with exponential backoff re-admission attempts and a quarantine buffer to prevent flapping.
- Exposes a small public API surface to define transient cohorts in rollout config (api/v1/rollouts.yaml and openapi updates).
- Example quickstart and k8s manifest for transient cohort experiment (examples/transient-cohort/).

Design details / safeguards: 
- Cohort TTLs are configurable but default to 15 minutes to encourage ephemeral experiments. Cohort assignment uses stable hashing of a request identifier + feature flag seed to keep membership stable for the TTL.
- SLO gates are evaluated over a sliding window with a minimum sample count (default 200 requests) before enforcement. Gates defined: p95 latency relative to baseline (default 1.25x), error-rate delta (absolute 0.5%).
- When a gate trips, requests are instantaneously routed to the baseline model and the cohort is moved to Quarantined state. Quarantine records persistent diagnostic metadata (recent traces, top-k failing example ids) to speed triage.
- Auto-heal uses an exponential cool-down (default 2m -> 4m -> 8m) and runs a dry-admit phase where 1% of traffic is tried against the candidate, gradually increasing if no regression is observed. Re-admittance requires passing the same SLO gates with a lower sample threshold.
- All state transitions are idempotent and store-backed, so controller restart does not lose cohort state.

Backward compatibility and API: 
- Rollout config additions are optional and backward-compatible. If a rollout does not declare transient cohorts, behavior is unchanged.
- The runtime falls back to baseline model using existing routing primitives; no changes required to model binaries.

Testing and verification: 
- Unit tests for controller state machine and hash stability (pkg/rollout/*_test.go).
- Integration tests that run two model variants in the perf-canary harness with injected latency/failure signals to ensure SLO gates trip and fallback occurs. These live under eval-harness/integration/transient-cohort.
- E2E smoke quickstart that deploys the example and runs a synthetic load generator to validate auto-heal behavior.
- Manual canary in staging for 24 hours with controlled ramp to 5% of traffic.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main as feature-flag guarded and disabled by default.
2) Deploy to staging; run automated integration/smoke tests (already executed in CI).
3) Enable for internal traffic via feature flag for 24h. Monitor SLOs and quarantine logs.
4) If stable, allow product teams to enable ephemeral experiments in prod at low traffic (<=1%) and use the quarantined diagnostic payload for triage.

Rollback / incident playbook:
- Immediate: feature flag off (instant stop). Because fallback is immediate, traffic will continue to baseline model with no client-visible errors.
- If cohort quarantines spike, controllers emit an alert (pager) and attach the diagnostic blob; SRE can inspect top failing examples and reopen with a tighter SLO or roll back via the feature flag.

Notes on operation cost and limits:
- Additional memory for cohort state is modest (per-cohort record ~1 KB). Default retention of quarantined records is 24h; configurable.
- Metrics cardinality is kept low by aggregating gates per-rollout+cohort_bucket; we avoid tagging by user id.

Related work / differences from existing primitives:
- Unlike staged canaries (longer lived, percentage-based) this primitive targets ephemeral experiments with fast TTL and automatic healing.
- Unlike shadow testing, this is in-path with immediate, enforced fallbacks when SLOs degrade.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests added and passing.
- [x] Integration tests added to eval harness.
- [x] Quickstart example included.
- [x] Docs draft added to redwood-docs (docs/rollouts/transient-cohorts.md).
- [x] Feature guarded and disabled by default.

Open questions / future work:
- Add adaptive sample-count thresholds that scale with request volume per-customer.
- Add richer diagnostic payload redaction for PII in quarantined traces.

review_comments: Ethan Morales (2026-02-22): Can we make the default cohort TTL shorter (10m) for low-volume customers? Response: Priya: kept at 15m as a conservative default but added a per-rollout override and documented tradeoffs.
Sandra Liu (2026-02-24): How do we ensure quarantine payloads do not contain PII? Priya: added redaction hook to quarantine recorder and a config knob to enforce redaction at collection time.
Marco Giannini (2026-02-26): Auto-heal backoff parameters seem aggressive; suggest smaller increments. Priya: adjusted to 2m/4m/8m and added config to control backoff base and multiplier.
release_notes: Add transient cohort rollout primitive: ephemeral cohort assignment, SLO-aware immediate fallback, quarantine diagnostics, and auto-heal. Feature is disabled by default and must be enabled per-rollout. See docs/rollouts/transient-cohorts.md for usage.
notes: This PR was merged after addressing reviewer comments and CI flakiness in integration tests. The feature is behind a runtime feature flag and is safe to ship to main.
incident_context: No incidents in prod during staged rollout. Staging experienced expected quarantines during simulated fault injection which validated fallback logic.
